llcFilesWith: Vermont Secretary of State (Assumed Business Name Registration, filed by a business organization under 11 V.S.A. § 1653)
soleProprietorFilesWith: Vermont Secretary of State (the same statewide assumed business name registry; individuals, partnerships, and unincorporated nonprofit associations register under 11 V.S.A. § 1621)
feeBasis: The Secretary of State fee to register an assumed business name is $70 under 11 V.S.A. § 1625(a); reregistration every five years costs $65 under § 1635(a). Online filing carries no extra fee.
renewalRule: A registrant must reregister every five years, filing with the Secretary of State no sooner than 60 days before the current registration or last reregistration expires, for a $65 fee (11 V.S.A. § 1635(a)). If the reregistration is not made, the name is open to the first person who applies for an original registration (§ 1635(b)).
protectionNote: An assumed business name discloses the name a business trades under and grants no exclusive right to it. It is screened, however: under 11 V.S.A. § 1621(c) the Secretary of State declines a business name unless it is distinguishable in the records from every other name registered or reserved with the office, so a live registration does block a later confusingly similar filing.
searchNote: Registered assumed business names appear in the Secretary of State's online business search. Only registrations with a status of Active, Terminated, Expiration Pending, Registered, Reserved, or Hold are counted when the office tests distinguishability.
notes: Vermont registers assumed business names statewide with the Secretary of State (11 V.S.A. ch. 15). Since 2025 Act 10, effective 2025-07-01, an LLC or other business organization registers under § 1653 in subchapter 3, while § 1621 covers individuals, partnerships, and unincorporated nonprofit associations; both file the same $70 registration and the state charges no extra fee for filing online. Section 1621(b) requires the registration to be filed no later than 10 days after business commences, and § 1628(a) requires a certificate of cessation within 10 days of stopping. Failure to register is not a nullity but it is expensive: under § 1626 an unregistered business may not maintain an action, counterclaim, crossclaim, or affirmative defense in Vermont until it registers, and it is liable to the State for $50 per day up to $10,000 per year plus the fees it should have paid. C.V.R. 04-020-001, Rule 3(b) additionally bars an assumed business name that uses a business entity identifier such as Company, Co., Limited, or Ltd., that implies governmental affiliation, or that consists merely of a registrant's own proper name. There is no publication requirement, and registration is disclosure rather than a trademark, so it grants no exclusive right. 2025 Act 10 also repealed §§ 1621a, 1623, 1624, 1627, and 1629 to 1634; the Secretary of State's fee schedule and name-rules page still cite several of those repealed sections, so read the statute for the operative rule.
